limits: Static, reduced-resolution meshes from one adult male model. Ligaments are modeled as whole structures (for example, UCL bundles are not separated). Not modeled: coracoacromial ligament, lateral ulnar collateral ligament, patellar ligament, spinal ligaments, nerves. The lateral ankle ligaments (ATFL, CFL, PTFL) and the ankle joint axes are not in the atlas, so they are drawn as simple bands. Cards summarise standard references; they are not a diagnosis tool and have not had independent expert review.

structures.name: Glenohumeral joint
structures.classification: Synovial ball-and-socket joint between the humeral head and the glenoid fossa.
structures.motion: Three degrees of freedom: flexion–extension, abduction–adduction, internal–external rotation.
structures.stabilizers: Static: glenoid labrum, capsule, glenohumeral and coracohumeral ligaments, negative joint pressure. Dynamic: rotator cuff, long head of biceps, deltoid and scapular position.
structures.baseball: Throwers usually show more external rotation and less internal rotation on the throwing side. The total arc and the side-to-side difference matter more than either number alone.
structures.note: The mesh shown is the joint capsule.

structures.name: Glenoid labrum
structures.attachments: Fibrocartilage rim attached around the glenoid margin. Superiorly it blends with the long head of biceps tendon.
structures.function: Deepens and widens the socket, adds to concavity–compression and anchors the glenohumeral ligaments.
structures.baseball: Superior labral (SLAP) lesions are common in overhead throwers. The "peel-back" model links them to biceps tension in abduction with maximal external rotation (late cocking).

structures.name: Superior glenohumeral ligament
structures.attachments: Anterosuperior glenoid and labrum, near the biceps origin, to the humerus just above the lesser tubercle.
structures.function: Limits inferior translation and external rotation with the arm at the side. Part of the rotator interval.
structures.baseball: Matters most with the arm adducted; contributes little in the 90° abducted throwing position.

structures.name: Middle glenohumeral ligament
structures.attachments: Anterior glenoid and labrum to the anatomical neck, medial to the lesser tubercle.
structures.function: Limits anterior translation and external rotation in mid-range abduction (around 45°).
structures.baseball: Highly variable: it can be thin, cord-like or absent. Do not expect the same picture in every athlete.

structures.name: Inferior glenohumeral ligament complex
structures.attachments: Inferior glenoid and labrum to the anatomical neck. Anterior band, axillary pouch and posterior band act like a hammock under the head.
structures.function: Main static restraint at 90° abduction. The anterior band tightens in abduction with external rotation; the posterior band tightens in abduction with internal rotation.
structures.baseball: Late cocking (abduction plus maximal external rotation) loads the anterior band. A thick, tight posteroinferior capsule is one proposed driver of internal-rotation loss (GIRD); treat that as a model, not settled fact.
structures.note: The mesh models the complex as one structure; the bands are not separated.

structures.name: Coracohumeral ligament
structures.attachments: Lateral base of the coracoid process to the greater and lesser tubercles, blending with the capsule and supraspinatus/subscapularis tendons.
structures.function: Limits inferior translation and external rotation with the arm at the side; roofs the rotator interval.
structures.baseball: A stiff rotator interval limits external rotation at the side, a different picture from the abducted-ER gain throwers show.

structures.name: Transverse humeral ligament
structures.attachments: Spans the intertubercular groove between the greater and lesser tubercles.
structures.function: Holds the long head of biceps tendon in the groove, with help from subscapularis and the coracohumeral ligament.
structures.baseball: Biceps instability in the groove usually involves the subscapularis and the pulley, not this band alone.

structures.name: Subacromial–subdeltoid bursa
structures.attachments: Between the acromion, coracoacromial arch and deltoid above, and the supraspinatus tendon and humeral head below.
structures.function: Lets the cuff glide under the arch.
structures.baseball: In throwers, posterosuperior (internal) impingement inside the joint is a separate mechanism from subacromial impingement under the arch.
structures.note: The coracoacromial ligament is not modeled in this atlas.

structures.name: Supraspinatus
structures.origin: Supraspinous fossa of the scapula.
structures.insertion: Superior facet of the greater tubercle.
structures.action: Abduction (with deltoid) and compression of the humeral head into the glenoid.
structures.baseball: Undersurface tears of the supraspinatus–infraspinatus junction are a classic finding with internal impingement in throwers.

structures.name: Infraspinatus
structures.origin: Infraspinous fossa of the scapula.
structures.insertion: Middle facet of the greater tubercle.
structures.action: External rotation; posterior stability of the humeral head.
structures.baseball: With teres minor, works eccentrically to slow internal rotation and horizontal adduction after ball release.

structures.name: Teres minor
structures.origin: Upper two-thirds of the lateral border of the scapula.
structures.insertion: Inferior facet of the greater tubercle.
structures.action: External rotation; posterior stability.
structures.baseball: Part of the posterior "brake" in deceleration; often trained with infraspinatus.

structures.name: Subscapularis
structures.origin: Subscapular fossa on the anterior scapula.
structures.insertion: Lesser tubercle of the humerus.
structures.action: Internal rotation; anterior stability, especially low in the range.
structures.baseball: Active in acceleration as the arm whips into internal rotation.

structures.name: Deltoid · anterior (clavicular) part
structures.origin: Lateral third of the clavicle.
structures.insertion: Deltoid tuberosity of the humerus.
structures.action: Flexion, internal rotation and horizontal adduction.

structures.name: Deltoid · middle (acromial) part
structures.origin: Lateral border of the acromion.
structures.insertion: Deltoid tuberosity of the humerus.
structures.action: Abduction.
structures.baseball: Holds the arm at shoulder height through the delivery; needs the cuff to keep the head centered.

structures.name: Deltoid · posterior (spinal) part
meshes: Scapular spinal part of deltoid muscle.r
structures.origin: Spine of the scapula.
structures.insertion: Deltoid tuberosity of the humerus.
structures.action: Extension, external rotation and horizontal abduction.
structures.baseball: Contributes to slowing the arm in follow-through.

structures.name: Pectoralis major · clavicular head
meshes: Clavicular head of pectoralis major muscle.r
structures.origin: Medial half of the clavicle.
structures.insertion: Lateral lip of the intertubercular groove.
structures.action: Flexion, horizontal adduction and internal rotation.

structures.name: Pectoralis major · sternocostal head
meshes: Sternocostal head of pectoralis major muscle.r
structures.origin: Sternum, upper six costal cartilages and the external oblique aponeurosis.
structures.insertion: Lateral lip of the intertubercular groove.
structures.action: Adduction, internal rotation, and extension from a flexed position.
structures.baseball: One of the main internal rotators that drives the arm forward in acceleration.

structures.name: Latissimus dorsi
structures.origin: Spinous processes T7–T12, thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest and lower 3–4 ribs.
structures.insertion: Floor of the intertubercular groove.
structures.action: Extension, adduction and internal rotation; links the pelvis and trunk to the arm.
structures.baseball: Highly active in acceleration. Latissimus and teres major strains are reported in professional pitchers.

structures.name: Teres major
structures.origin: Posterior surface near the inferior angle of the scapula.
structures.insertion: Medial lip of the intertubercular groove.
structures.action: Extension, adduction and internal rotation.
structures.baseball: Works with latissimus; often injured with it in pitchers.

structures.name: Biceps brachii · long head
structures.origin: Supraglenoid tubercle and superior labrum.
structures.insertion: Radial tuberosity and bicipital aponeurosis.
structures.action: Elbow flexion and supination; tendon helps depress and steady the humeral head.
structures.baseball: Its anchor on the superior labrum is where the peel-back mechanism acts. Also slows elbow extension in follow-through.

structures.name: Biceps brachii · short head
structures.origin: Tip of the coracoid process.
structures.insertion: Radial tuberosity and bicipital aponeurosis.
structures.action: Elbow flexion and supination; weak shoulder flexion.

structures.name: Coracobrachialis
structures.origin: Tip of the coracoid process.
structures.insertion: Medial shaft of the humerus near its midpoint.
structures.action: Flexion and adduction.

structures.name: Triceps brachii · long head
structures.origin: Infraglenoid tubercle of the scapula.
structures.insertion: Olecranon of the ulna.
structures.action: Elbow extension; shoulder extension and adduction.
structures.baseball: Crosses both shoulder and elbow; tight long head limits overhead flexion with the elbow bent.

structures.name: Scapulothoracic articulation
structures.classification: Functional (not true synovial) articulation: the scapula glides on the rib cage, guided by the AC and SC joints.
structures.motion: Upward/downward rotation, posterior/anterior tilt, internal/external rotation, elevation/depression, protraction/retraction.
structures.stabilizers: Serratus anterior and trapezius force couple, rhomboids, levator scapulae, pectoralis minor; the clavicle as a strut.
structures.baseball: Scapular upward rotation and posterior tilt keep the subacromial space and glenoid aligned under the humerus at arm cocking. Altered motion ("dyskinesis") is common and not always symptomatic.
structures.note: No mesh: this articulation has no capsule.

structures.name: Acromioclavicular joint
structures.classification: Synovial plane joint between the lateral clavicle and the acromion, often with an incomplete disc.
structures.motion: Small rotations and glides that let the scapula rotate and tilt on the clavicle.
structures.stabilizers: AC ligament (horizontal), coracoclavicular ligaments (vertical), deltotrapezial fascia.
structures.baseball: Falls on the shoulder while diving or sliding are the usual mechanism of AC sprains in fielders.
structures.note: The mesh shows the capsule and disc.

structures.name: Sternoclavicular joint
structures.classification: Synovial saddle joint with an articular disc between the medial clavicle, manubrium and first costal cartilage.
structures.motion: Elevation–depression, protraction–retraction and long-axis rotation of the clavicle.
structures.closePacked: Full arm elevation (maximal posterior clavicular rotation).
structures.stabilizers: Anterior and posterior SC ligaments, interclavicular and costoclavicular ligaments, articular disc.
structures.baseball: The only bony link between the arm and the axial skeleton.

structures.name: Acromioclavicular ligament
structures.attachments: Lateral clavicle to the acromion over the AC joint capsule.
structures.function: Main restraint to horizontal (anteroposterior) AC translation.

structures.name: Conoid ligament (coracoclavicular)
structures.attachments: Base of the coracoid process to the conoid tubercle on the underside of the clavicle.
structures.function: Limits superior displacement of the clavicle; couples clavicular rotation to scapular motion.
structures.baseball: Torn in higher-grade AC separations.

structures.name: Trapezoid ligament (coracoclavicular)
structures.attachments: Upper surface of the coracoid to the trapezoid line of the clavicle.
structures.function: Limits superior and medial displacement of the clavicle on the acromion.
structures.baseball: Torn in higher-grade AC separations.

structures.name: Sternoclavicular ligaments (anterior and posterior)
structures.attachments: Medial clavicle to the manubrium, in front of and behind the joint.
structures.function: Limit anterior and posterior translation of the medial clavicle; the posterior ligament is the stronger restraint.

structures.name: Trapezius · upper (descending) part
structures.origin: External occipital protuberance, nuchal ligament.
structures.insertion: Lateral third of the clavicle.
structures.action: Scapular elevation and upward rotation (via the clavicle).
structures.innervation: Accessory nerve (CN XI); C3–C4 sensory/proprioceptive fibers.
structures.baseball: Part of the upward-rotation force couple with lower trapezius and serratus anterior.

structures.name: Trapezius · middle (transverse) part
structures.origin: Spinous processes C7–T3 (approximately).
structures.insertion: Acromion and spine of the scapula.
structures.action: Retraction (and external rotation) of the scapula.
structures.baseball: Holds the scapula back as the trunk rotates forward in the delivery.

structures.name: Trapezius · lower (ascending) part
structures.origin: Spinous processes of the middle and lower thoracic vertebrae (about T4–T12).
structures.insertion: Root (medial end) of the scapular spine.
structures.action: Depression, upward rotation and posterior tilt of the scapula.
structures.baseball: Often a training target in throwers to support upward rotation and posterior tilt.

structures.name: Rhomboid major
structures.origin: Spinous processes T2–T5.
structures.insertion: Medial border of the scapula below the spine.
structures.action: Retraction and downward rotation; holds the scapula to the thorax.
structures.baseball: Works eccentrically to control scapular protraction in follow-through.

structures.name: Rhomboid minor
structures.origin: Nuchal ligament and spinous processes C7–T1.
structures.insertion: Medial border of the scapula at the root of the spine.
structures.action: Retraction and downward rotation.

structures.name: Levator scapulae
structures.origin: Transverse processes C1–C4.
structures.insertion: Medial border of the scapula from the superior angle to the spine.
structures.action: Elevation and downward rotation of the scapula.

structures.name: Serratus anterior
structures.origin: Outer surfaces of ribs 1–8 or 9.
structures.insertion: Costal (anterior) surface of the medial border of the scapula.
structures.action: Protraction, upward rotation and posterior tilt; keeps the scapula on the thorax.
structures.baseball: Key upward rotator through cocking and acceleration. Weakness shows as medial-border prominence.

structures.name: Pectoralis minor
structures.origin: Ribs 3–5 near their costal cartilages.
structures.insertion: Medial border of the coracoid process.
structures.action: Anterior tilt, internal rotation and depression of the scapula.
structures.baseball: A short pec minor is linked to reduced posterior tilt; length is hard to measure reliably.

structures.name: Subclavius
structures.origin: First rib and its costal cartilage.
structures.insertion: Underside of the middle third of the clavicle.
structures.action: Depresses and steadies the clavicle at the SC joint.

structures.name: Elbow joint complex
structures.classification: Compound synovial joint: humeroulnar (hinge), humeroradial, and proximal radioulnar (pivot) in one capsule.
structures.motion: Two degrees of freedom: flexion–extension and pronation–supination.
structures.stabilizers: Bony fit of the olecranon in its fossa (in extension), UCL anterior bundle (valgus), lateral collateral complex and annular ligament (varus and posterolateral), flexor–pronator mass (dynamic valgus support).
structures.baseball: Late cocking and early acceleration put a large valgus load on the elbow. Many pitchers lose a few degrees of extension on the throwing side.
structures.note: The mesh shows the joint capsule.

structures.name: Ulnar (medial) collateral ligament
structures.attachments: Anterior bundle: anteroinferior medial epicondyle to the sublime tubercle of the ulna. Posterior and transverse bundles complete the complex.
structures.function: The anterior bundle is the primary restraint to valgus load from about 20° to 120° of flexion.
structures.baseball: Peak elbow varus torque in late cocking (Fleisig 1995) exceeds isolated cadaveric UCL failure loads, so the flexor–pronator muscles are thought to share the load. The UCL is the structure repaired or reconstructed in "Tommy John" surgery.
structures.note: Modeled as one structure; the anterior, posterior and transverse bundles are not separated.

structures.name: Radial (lateral) collateral ligament
structures.attachments: Lateral epicondyle to the annular ligament.
structures.function: Resists varus load; part of the lateral collateral complex with the lateral ulnar collateral ligament.
structures.baseball: The lateral ulnar collateral band (main restraint to posterolateral rotatory instability) is not modeled separately.

structures.name: Annular ligament of radius
structures.attachments: Anterior and posterior margins of the radial notch of the ulna, encircling the radial head.
structures.function: Holds the radial head against the ulna while it spins in pronation and supination.

structures.name: Interosseous membrane of forearm
structures.attachments: Interosseous borders of the radius and ulna. Central fibers run distal and medial from radius to ulna.
structures.function: Transfers compressive load from the radius to the ulna and separates the anterior and posterior compartments.

structures.name: Pronator teres
structures.origin: Humeral head: medial epicondyle (common flexor origin). Ulnar head: coronoid process.
structures.insertion: Middle of the lateral radius.
structures.action: Pronation; assists elbow flexion.
structures.baseball: Part of the flexor–pronator mass over the medial elbow; pronation continues through ball release.
structures.note: Both heads are selected together.

structures.name: Flexor carpi ulnaris
meshes: Humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris.r
Ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris.r
structures.origin: Humeral head: medial epicondyle. Ulnar head: olecranon and posterior border of the ulna.
structures.insertion: Pisiform, with ligamentous continuity to the hamate and fifth metacarpal.
structures.action: Wrist flexion and ulnar deviation.
structures.baseball: Sits directly over the UCL anterior bundle. Cadaver work suggests it and FDS give the most dynamic valgus support. The ulnar nerve passes between its two heads.
structures.note: Both heads are selected together.

structures.name: Flexor digitorum superficialis
meshes: Humero-ulnar head of flexor digitorum superficialis.r
Radial head of flexor digitorum superficialis.r
structures.origin: Humeroulnar head: medial epicondyle and coronoid process. Radial head: anterior oblique line of the radius.
structures.insertion: Sides of the middle phalanges of digits 2–5.
structures.action: Flexes the PIP and MCP joints and the wrist.
structures.baseball: With FCU, the main dynamic support over the UCL. Grip and finger flexion are trained partly for this reason.

structures.name: Flexor carpi radialis
structures.origin: Medial epicondyle (common flexor origin).
structures.insertion: Bases of the 2nd and 3rd metacarpals.
structures.action: Wrist flexion and radial deviation.

structures.name: Palmaris longus
structures.origin: Medial epicondyle (common flexor origin).
structures.insertion: Flexor retinaculum and palmar aponeurosis.
structures.action: Weak wrist flexion; tenses the palmar fascia.
structures.baseball: Absent in a share of people. When present, its tendon is a common graft for UCL reconstruction.

structures.name: Flexor digitorum profundus
structures.origin: Anterior and medial ulna and the interosseous membrane.
structures.insertion: Bases of the distal phalanges of digits 2–5.
structures.action: Flexes the DIP joints, then the other finger joints and the wrist.
structures.innervation: Medial part: ulnar nerve. Lateral part: anterior interosseous branch of the median nerve (C8–T1).

structures.name: Pronator quadratus
structures.origin: Distal quarter of the anterior ulna.
structures.insertion: Distal quarter of the anterior radius.
structures.action: Primary pronator; holds the distal radioulnar joint together.

structures.name: Biceps brachii (both heads)
structures.origin: Long head: supraglenoid tubercle. Short head: coracoid tip.
structures.insertion: Radial tuberosity and bicipital aponeurosis.
structures.action: Elbow flexion and forearm supination (strongest with the elbow flexed).
structures.baseball: Works eccentrically to slow elbow extension after ball release.
structures.note: Both heads are selected together. See the shoulder region for each head.

structures.name: Brachialis
structures.origin: Distal half of the anterior humerus.
structures.insertion: Coronoid process and ulnar tuberosity.
structures.action: Elbow flexion in every forearm position.
structures.innervation: Musculocutaneous nerve (C5–C6), small lateral part from the radial nerve.
structures.baseball: The workhorse elbow flexor; also decelerates elbow extension.

structures.name: Brachioradialis
structures.origin: Lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus.
structures.insertion: Radial styloid process.
structures.action: Elbow flexion, strongest in mid-pronation.

structures.name: Triceps brachii (three heads)
structures.origin: Long head: infraglenoid tubercle. Lateral head: posterior humerus above the radial groove. Medial head: posterior humerus below the radial groove.
structures.insertion: Olecranon of the ulna.
structures.action: Elbow extension; long head also extends and adducts the shoulder.
structures.baseball: Drives elbow extension in acceleration. Valgus extension overload loads the posteromedial olecranon at the same time.
structures.note: All three heads are selected together.

structures.name: Anconeus
structures.origin: Posterior lateral epicondyle.
structures.insertion: Lateral olecranon and upper posterior ulna.
structures.action: Assists extension; steadies the ulna in pronation.

structures.name: Supinator
structures.origin: Lateral epicondyle, radial collateral and annular ligaments, supinator crest of the ulna.
structures.insertion: Lateral, posterior and anterior proximal third of the radius.
structures.action: Supination.
structures.innervation: Deep branch of the radial nerve / posterior interosseous nerve (C6–C7).
structures.baseball: The posterior interosseous nerve passes through it.

structures.name: Extensor carpi radialis longus
structures.origin: Lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus.
structures.insertion: Base of the 2nd metacarpal.
structures.action: Wrist extension and radial deviation.

structures.name: Extensor carpi radialis brevis
structures.origin: Lateral epicondyle (common extensor origin).
structures.insertion: Base of the 3rd metacarpal.
structures.action: Wrist extension.
structures.innervation: Deep branch of the radial nerve (C7–C8).
structures.baseball: The usual site of lateral epicondylopathy; in baseball more common in hitters than throwers.

structures.name: Extensor digitorum
structures.origin: Lateral epicondyle (common extensor origin).
structures.insertion: Extensor expansions of digits 2–5.
structures.action: Extends the fingers and assists wrist extension.

structures.name: Extensor carpi ulnaris
meshes: Humeral head of extensor carpi ulnaris.r
Ulnar head of extensor carpi ulnaris.r
structures.origin: Lateral epicondyle and posterior border of the ulna.
structures.insertion: Base of the 5th metacarpal.
structures.action: Wrist extension and ulnar deviation.
structures.baseball: ECU tendon subluxation at the wrist is reported in hitters, usually on the bottom (lead) hand.
structures.note: Both heads are selected together.

structures.name: Lumbar spine (disc and facet joints)
structures.classification: Each level combines an intervertebral disc (cartilaginous) and two facet joints (synovial plane).
structures.motion: Mostly flexion–extension; facet orientation limits axial rotation to a few degrees per level.
structures.stabilizers: Discs, facet capsules, anterior and posterior longitudinal ligaments, ligamentum flavum, interspinous ligaments, multifidus.
structures.baseball: Most trunk rotation in throwing and hitting must come from the hips and thoracic spine. Repeated extension with rotation is a proposed mechanism for pars stress injuries in young players.
structures.note: Spinal ligaments are not modeled in this atlas.

structures.name: Thoracic spine and rib joints
structures.classification: Disc and facet joints plus costovertebral and costotransverse joints with the ribs.
structures.motion: Rotation and extension, more freely than the lumbar spine; ribs elevate and rotate in breathing.
structures.stabilizers: Rib cage, discs, facet capsules, costal ligaments.
structures.baseball: Thoracic rotation and extension supply much of hip–shoulder separation and the layback of the arm.
structures.note: No mesh.

structures.name: Sacroiliac joint
structures.classification: Synovial (anterior) and fibrous (posterior) joint between the sacrum and ilium.
structures.motion: A few degrees of nutation and counternutation.
structures.stabilizers: Interosseous, posterior and anterior SI ligaments, sacrotuberous and sacrospinous ligaments, thoracolumbar fascia.
structures.baseball: Transfers force from the legs into the trunk on every stride.
structures.note: The mesh shows the SI ligaments that wrap the joint.

structures.name: Iliolumbar ligament
structures.attachments: Transverse process of L5 (sometimes L4) to the posterior iliac crest.
structures.function: Limits motion of L5 on the sacrum, especially lateral flexion and rotation.

structures.name: Sacrotuberous ligament
structures.attachments: Posterior ilium, sacrum and coccyx to the ischial tuberosity.
structures.function: Resists nutation of the sacrum.
structures.baseball: Some biceps femoris long head fibers continue into it, a link between the hamstrings and the pelvis.

structures.name: Thoracolumbar fascia · posterior layer
structures.attachments: Spinous processes and supraspinous ligaments to the iliac crest and sacrum.
structures.function: Encloses the erector spinae; connects latissimus dorsi to the opposite gluteus maximus.
structures.baseball: A proposed path for force between the hip and the opposite arm.

structures.name: External oblique
structures.origin: Outer surfaces of ribs 5–12.
structures.insertion: Linea alba, pubic tubercle and anterior half of the iliac crest.
structures.action: Contralateral trunk rotation, trunk flexion, ipsilateral side bending.
structures.innervation: Thoracoabdominal nerves T7–T11 and subcostal nerve T12.
structures.baseball: Oblique strains are common in baseball and occur mostly on the side opposite the throwing arm (lead side in hitters).
structures.note: Rotation pairs the external oblique of one side with the internal oblique of the other. This atlas shows the right side only.

structures.name: Internal oblique
structures.origin: Thoracolumbar fascia, anterior two-thirds of the iliac crest, lateral inguinal ligament.
structures.insertion: Lower borders of ribs 10–12, linea alba, pubic crest.
structures.action: Ipsilateral trunk rotation, trunk flexion, side bending.
structures.innervation: Thoracoabdominal nerves T7–T12, iliohypogastric and ilioinguinal nerves (L1).

structures.name: Rectus abdominis
structures.origin: Pubic crest and symphysis.
structures.insertion: Xiphoid process and costal cartilages 5–7.
structures.action: Trunk flexion; resists trunk extension.
structures.baseball: Strains of the rectus abdominis on the non-throwing side have been described in pitchers; it resists the arched trunk position before acceleration.

structures.name: Transversus abdominis
structures.origin: Costal cartilages 7–12, thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest, lateral inguinal ligament.
structures.insertion: Linea alba and pubic crest.
structures.action: Compresses the abdomen; tensions the thoracolumbar fascia.

structures.name: Quadratus lumborum
structures.origin: Iliac crest and iliolumbar ligament.
structures.insertion: 12th rib and transverse processes L1–L4.
structures.action: Side bending; steadies the 12th rib; elevates the pelvis on one side.

structures.name: Iliocostalis lumborum (erector spinae)
structures.origin: Common erector spinae tendon: iliac crest, sacrum, lumbar spinous processes.
structures.insertion: Angles of the lower 6–8 ribs.
structures.action: Trunk extension and side bending.

structures.name: Longissimus thoracis (erector spinae)
structures.origin: Common erector spinae tendon and lumbar transverse processes.
structures.insertion: Thoracic transverse processes and adjacent ribs.
structures.action: Trunk extension and side bending.

structures.name: Multifidus (lumbar)
structures.origin: Sacrum, posterior superior iliac spine, mammillary processes of lumbar vertebrae.
structures.insertion: Spinous processes two to four levels above.
structures.action: Segmental extension and control of rotation and shear.
structures.innervation: Medial branches of the dorsal rami.

structures.name: Hip joint
structures.classification: Synovial ball-and-socket joint between the femoral head and the acetabulum.
structures.motion: Three degrees of freedom: flexion–extension, abduction–adduction, internal–external rotation.
structures.closePacked: Full extension with slight internal rotation and abduction.
structures.stabilizers: Deep acetabulum and labrum, iliofemoral, pubofemoral and ischiofemoral ligaments, deep hip rotators, gluteus medius and minimus.
structures.baseball: The lead hip must internally rotate as the pelvis turns over a planted leg; the back hip drives extension and rotation. Hip rotation deficits are commonly screened in pitchers.
structures.note: The mesh shows the joint capsule.

structures.name: Acetabular labrum
structures.attachments: Rim of the acetabulum, completed inferiorly by the transverse acetabular ligament.
structures.function: Deepens the socket and seals the joint fluid layer.
structures.baseball: Labral tears and femoroacetabular impingement occur in baseball players; they reduce hip rotation used in rotation-dominant tasks.

structures.name: Iliofemoral ligament ("Y ligament")
structures.attachments: Anterior inferior iliac spine and acetabular rim to the intertrochanteric line.
structures.function: Strongest hip ligament. Limits extension; its lateral (transverse) band also limits external rotation.
structures.baseball: Tight in the trail leg at full hip extension at foot strike.
structures.note: Both bands are selected together.

structures.name: Pubofemoral ligament
structures.attachments: Superior pubic ramus to the inferior capsule and femoral neck.
structures.function: Limits abduction and extension; some external rotation.

structures.name: Ischiofemoral ligament
structures.attachments: Posterior acetabular rim (ischium) spiraling to the femoral neck near the greater trochanter.
structures.function: Limits internal rotation and extension; also adduction in flexion.
structures.baseball: Tightens as the lead hip internally rotates in late stride and acceleration.

structures.name: Iliotibial tract
structures.attachments: Iliac crest (via tensor fasciae latae and gluteus maximus) to the lateral tibial condyle (Gerdy tubercle).
structures.function: Transmits TFL and gluteus maximus force down the lateral thigh; lateral knee stabilizer.

structures.name: Gluteus maximus
structures.origin: Posterior ilium, sacrum, coccyx, sacrotuberous ligament and thoracolumbar fascia.
structures.insertion: Iliotibial tract and gluteal tuberosity of the femur.
structures.action: Hip extension and external rotation; upper fibers abduct.
structures.baseball: Drives the back-leg push and decelerates the lead leg as the body moves over it.

structures.name: Gluteus medius
structures.origin: Outer ilium between the anterior and posterior gluteal lines.
structures.insertion: Lateral facet of the greater trochanter.
structures.action: Hip abduction; anterior fibers internally rotate, posterior fibers externally rotate; stabilizes the pelvis in single-leg stance.
structures.baseball: Controls the pelvis on the stance leg during leg lift and the stride.

structures.name: Gluteus minimus
structures.origin: Outer ilium between the anterior and inferior gluteal lines.
structures.insertion: Anterior facet of the greater trochanter.
structures.action: Hip abduction and internal rotation; steadies the femoral head.

structures.name: Tensor fasciae latae
structures.origin: Anterior superior iliac spine and anterior iliac crest.
structures.insertion: Iliotibial tract.
structures.action: Hip flexion, abduction and internal rotation; tensions the IT tract.

structures.name: Piriformis
structures.origin: Anterior surface of the sacrum.
structures.insertion: Upper border of the greater trochanter.
structures.action: External rotation of the extended hip; abducts the flexed hip.
structures.baseball: The sciatic nerve usually exits just below it; anatomical variants exist.

structures.name: Superior gemellus
structures.origin: Ischial spine.
structures.insertion: Obturator internus tendon to the medial greater trochanter.
structures.action: External rotation.

structures.name: Obturator internus
structures.origin: Inner surface of the obturator membrane and surrounding bone.
structures.insertion: Medial surface of the greater trochanter.
structures.action: External rotation; steadies the femoral head.

structures.name: Inferior gemellus
structures.origin: Ischial tuberosity.
structures.insertion: Obturator internus tendon to the medial greater trochanter.
structures.action: External rotation.

structures.name: Quadratus femoris
structures.origin: Lateral border of the ischial tuberosity.
structures.insertion: Quadrate tubercle on the intertrochanteric crest.
structures.action: External rotation.

structures.name: Obturator externus
structures.origin: Outer surface of the obturator membrane and surrounding bone.
structures.insertion: Trochanteric fossa of the femur.
structures.action: External rotation.

structures.name: Iliacus (iliopsoas)
structures.origin: Iliac fossa.
structures.insertion: Lesser trochanter (with psoas major).
structures.action: Hip flexion.
structures.baseball: Pulls the lead leg through in the stride and the back leg through after release.

structures.name: Psoas major (iliopsoas)
structures.origin: Bodies and transverse processes T12–L5.
structures.insertion: Lesser trochanter.
structures.action: Hip flexion; contributes to lumbar stability.

structures.name: Adductor longus
structures.origin: Body of the pubis below the pubic crest.
structures.insertion: Middle third of the linea aspera.
structures.action: Hip adduction; assists flexion.
structures.baseball: Groin strains are frequent in baseball, often with lateral movement and base-running.

structures.name: Adductor brevis
structures.origin: Body and inferior ramus of the pubis.
structures.insertion: Upper linea aspera and pectineal line.
structures.action: Hip adduction.

structures.name: Adductor magnus
structures.origin: Inferior pubic ramus, ischial ramus and ischial tuberosity.
structures.insertion: Linea aspera and adductor tubercle.
structures.action: Adduction; the ischial ("hamstring") part extends the hip.
structures.innervation: Obturator nerve (adductor part) and tibial division of the sciatic nerve (hamstring part), L2–L4.

structures.name: Gracilis
structures.origin: Body and inferior ramus of the pubis.
structures.insertion: Medial proximal tibia (pes anserinus).
structures.action: Hip adduction, knee flexion and internal rotation.

structures.name: Pectineus
structures.origin: Pectineal line of the pubis.
structures.insertion: Pectineal line of the femur.
structures.action: Hip adduction and flexion.
structures.innervation: Femoral nerve (L2–L3), sometimes the obturator nerve.

structures.name: Sartorius
structures.origin: Anterior superior iliac spine.
structures.insertion: Medial proximal tibia (pes anserinus).
structures.action: Hip flexion, abduction and external rotation; knee flexion.

structures.name: Knee joint
structures.classification: Synovial modified hinge (tibiofemoral) plus the patellofemoral joint.
structures.motion: Flexion–extension, with internal–external rotation when flexed.
structures.closePacked: Full extension with tibial external rotation ("screw-home").
structures.stabilizers: Cruciate and collateral ligaments, menisci, posterolateral corner, quadriceps and hamstrings.
structures.baseball: The lead knee braces as it extends after foot strike; a firmer lead leg is linked to more energy transfer up the chain. Catchers load the knee in deep flexion.
structures.note: The mesh shows the joint capsule.

structures.name: Anterior cruciate ligament
structures.attachments: Medial wall of the lateral femoral condyle to the anterior intercondylar area of the tibia.
structures.function: Limits anterior tibial translation and internal rotation; tight in extension.
structures.baseball: Non-contact ACL injuries happen in fielders and base-runners with cutting, landing and sudden deceleration.

structures.name: Posterior cruciate ligament
structures.attachments: Lateral wall of the medial femoral condyle to the posterior intercondylar area of the tibia.
structures.function: Limits posterior tibial translation, most in flexion.

structures.name: Tibial (medial) collateral ligament
meshes: Superficial part of tibial collateral ligament.r
Deep part of tibial collateral ligament.r
structures.attachments: Medial femoral epicondyle to the medial tibia; the deep part attaches to the medial meniscus.
structures.function: Primary restraint to valgus; also limits external rotation.
structures.baseball: Valgus-stress injury on slides and collisions at the bag.
structures.note: Superficial and deep parts are selected together.

structures.name: Fibular (lateral) collateral ligament
structures.attachments: Lateral femoral epicondyle to the fibular head.
structures.function: Primary restraint to varus; part of the posterolateral corner.

structures.name: Medial meniscus
structures.attachments: C-shaped fibrocartilage on the medial tibial plateau, firmly attached to the capsule and deep MCL.
structures.function: Spreads load, deepens the plateau, helps stability.
structures.baseball: Less mobile than the lateral meniscus, so more often torn with twisting under load. Catchers spend long periods in deep flexion.

structures.name: Lateral meniscus
structures.attachments: Nearly circular fibrocartilage on the lateral tibial plateau; loosely attached, separated from the LCL by the popliteus tendon.
structures.function: Spreads load; more mobile than the medial meniscus.

structures.name: Biceps femoris · long head
structures.origin: Ischial tuberosity.
structures.insertion: Primarily the fibular head; distal attachments also reach the lateral tibia.
structures.action: Hip extension, knee flexion, and external rotation of the flexed knee.
structures.innervation: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve.
structures.baseball: The most commonly strained hamstring, usually in sprinting (base-running), when it is long and absorbing force late in swing.

structures.name: Biceps femoris · short head
structures.origin: Lateral linea aspera of the femur.
structures.insertion: Distal biceps femoris attachment at the fibular head and lateral tibia.
structures.action: Knee flexion and external rotation; does not cross the hip.
structures.innervation: Common fibular division of the sciatic nerve.

structures.name: Semitendinosus
structures.origin: Ischial tuberosity; proximal connection with the long-head biceps tendon.
structures.insertion: Anteromedial proximal tibia at the pes anserinus.
structures.action: Hip extension, knee flexion, and internal rotation of the flexed knee.
structures.innervation: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve.

structures.name: Semimembranosus
structures.origin: Ischial tuberosity.
structures.insertion: Medial tibial condyle.
structures.action: Hip extension, knee flexion, and internal rotation of the flexed knee.
structures.innervation: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve.

structures.name: Rectus femoris
structures.origin: Anterior inferior iliac spine and the superior acetabular rim.
structures.insertion: Patella and, via the patellar ligament, the tibial tuberosity.
structures.action: Knee extension and hip flexion.
structures.baseball: The only quadriceps muscle crossing the hip; strains occur with sprinting and kicking-type actions.

structures.name: Vastus lateralis
structures.origin: Greater trochanter, intertrochanteric line and lateral linea aspera.
structures.insertion: Lateral patella and quadriceps tendon.
structures.action: Knee extension.

structures.name: Vastus medialis
structures.origin: Intertrochanteric line and medial linea aspera.
structures.insertion: Medial patella and quadriceps tendon.
structures.action: Knee extension; distal oblique fibers help track the patella.

structures.name: Vastus intermedius
structures.origin: Anterior and lateral femoral shaft.
structures.insertion: Deep quadriceps tendon to the patella.
structures.action: Knee extension.

structures.name: Gastrocnemius (both heads)
structures.origin: Medial and lateral femoral condyles.
structures.insertion: Calcaneus via the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon.
structures.action: Ankle plantarflexion; assists knee flexion.
structures.baseball: Medial head strains occur with explosive push-off.
structures.note: Both heads are selected together.

structures.name: Popliteus
structures.origin: Lateral femoral condyle and lateral meniscus.
structures.insertion: Posterior tibia above the soleal line.
structures.action: Unlocks the extended knee (internal rotation of the tibia); limits external rotation.

structures.name: Talus
structures.note: Shown for spatial context. Attachment footprints are described in the muscle and ligament cards, not marked on the mesh.

structures.name: Calcaneus
structures.note: Shown for spatial context. Attachment footprints are described in the muscle and ligament cards, not marked on the mesh.

structures.name: Navicular
structures.note: Shown for spatial context. Attachment footprints are described in the muscle and ligament cards, not marked on the mesh.

structures.name: Cuboid
structures.note: Shown for spatial context. Attachment footprints are described in the muscle and ligament cards, not marked on the mesh.

structures.name: Cuneiforms (medial, intermediate, lateral)
structures.note: Shown for spatial context. Attachment footprints are described in the muscle and ligament cards, not marked on the mesh.

structures.name: Metatarsals 1–5
structures.note: Shown for spatial context. Attachment footprints are described in the muscle and ligament cards, not marked on the mesh.

structures.name: Phalanges of the toes
meshes: Proximal phalanx of first finger of foot.r
Distal phalanx of first finger of foot.r
Proximal phalanx of second finger of foot.r
Middle phalanx of second finger of foot.r
Distal phalanx of second finger of foot.r
Proximal phalanx of third finger of foot.r
Middle phalanx of third finger of foot.r
Distal phalanx of third finger of foot.r
Proximal phalanx of fourth finger of foot.r
Middle phalanx of fourth finger of foot.r
Distal phalanx of fourth finger of foot.r
Proximal phalanx of fifth finger of foot.r
Middle phalanx of fifth finger of foot.r
Distal phalanx of fifth finger of foot.r
structures.note: Shown for spatial context. Attachment footprints are described in the muscle and ligament cards, not marked on the mesh.

structures.name: Talocrural (ankle) joint
structures.classification: Synovial hinge: the talus sits in the mortise formed by the tibia and fibula.
structures.motion: Dorsiflexion–plantarflexion about an oblique axis, so dorsiflexion also turns the foot slightly out and plantarflexion slightly in.
structures.closePacked: Full dorsiflexion (the wider front of the talus wedges into the mortise).
structures.stabilizers: Bony mortise, lateral ligaments (ATFL, CFL, PTFL), deltoid ligament and the syndesmosis.
structures.baseball: Drive-leg dorsiflexion while loading at the rubber, lead-ankle stability at foot strike, and catcher squat depth all depend on this joint.
structures.note: Shown as its axis: a line through the tips of the two malleoli. The lateral malleolus sits lower and further back than the medial one, which is why the axis is tilted.

structures.name: Subtalar joint
structures.classification: Synovial joint between the talus and calcaneus (posterior, middle and anterior facets).
structures.motion: Inversion–eversion; with the midfoot this gives supination–pronation.
structures.stabilizers: Interosseous talocalcaneal and cervical ligaments, calcaneofibular ligament, tibiocalcaneal part of the deltoid ligament.
structures.baseball: Lets the foot adapt to the slope of the mound and uneven ground; the lead foot pronates as it takes load after foot strike.
structures.note: Shown as its axis, which rises from the back-outer heel to the top-inner talar neck: about 40° from horizontal and 17° toward the midline in this model, close to published averages.

structures.name: Metatarsophalangeal (MTP) joints
structures.classification: Synovial condyloid joints between the metatarsal heads and the proximal phalanges.
structures.motion: Toe flexion–extension, with a little abduction–adduction.
structures.stabilizers: Plantar plates, collateral ligaments, and the two sesamoids under the first MTP.
structures.baseball: Big-toe extension is the last lever of drive-leg push-off and sprinting; catchers sit on extended toes.
structures.note: The mesh shows the joint capsules of all five MTP joints.

structures.name: Anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL)
structures.attachments: Anterior border of the lateral malleolus to the lateral neck of the talus.
structures.function: Limits forward slide of the talus and inversion, most when the foot is pointed down (plantarflexed). The weakest lateral ligament.
structures.baseball: The most commonly sprained ligament in the body: rolling the foot in on a base, a bag edge or uneven ground while running.
structures.note: The atlas has no mesh for this, so it is drawn as a simple band between its attachments.

structures.name: Calcaneofibular ligament (CFL)
structures.attachments: Tip of the lateral malleolus, down and back to the lateral calcaneus, deep to the fibular tendons.
structures.function: Limits inversion with the ankle neutral or dorsiflexed; it crosses both the ankle and the subtalar joint.
structures.baseball: Usually torn after the ATFL in a more severe inversion sprain.
structures.note: The atlas has no mesh for this, so it is drawn as a simple band between its attachments.

structures.name: Posterior talofibular ligament (PTFL)
structures.attachments: Malleolar fossa on the inner back of the lateral malleolus to the lateral tubercle of the posterior talar process.
structures.function: Limits backward slide and external rotation of the talus. The strongest of the three lateral ligaments; rarely torn alone.
structures.note: The atlas has no mesh for this, so it is drawn as a simple band between its attachments.

structures.name: Deltoid (medial collateral) ligament
structures.attachments: Medial malleolus fanning out to the navicular, the talus and the sustentaculum tali of the calcaneus.
structures.function: Limits eversion and outward shift of the talus; much stronger than the lateral ligaments.
structures.baseball: Injured with eversion and external-rotation twists, often together with the syndesmosis.
structures.note: Tibionavicular, tibiocalcaneal and posterior tibiotalar parts are selected together; the deep anterior tibiotalar part is not in the atlas.

structures.name: Distal tibiofibular syndesmosis
structures.attachments: Anterior and posterior tibiofibular ligaments, the transverse ligament and the interosseous ligament binding the distal tibia and fibula.
structures.function: Holds the ankle mortise together; it is stretched as the wider front of the talus enters the mortise in dorsiflexion.
structures.baseball: A "high ankle sprain": the foot is forced into external rotation, for example when a cleat catches on a slide or a cut. Return to play usually takes longer than for a lateral sprain.
structures.note: Anterior, posterior and transverse ligaments are selected together.

structures.name: Interosseous membrane of the leg
structures.attachments: Interosseous borders of the tibia and fibula.
structures.function: Attachment for the deep calf and anterior compartment muscles; ties the two leg bones together and continues into the syndesmosis.

structures.name: Calcaneal (Achilles) tendon
structures.attachments: Joins gastrocnemius and soleus (often with plantaris) to the middle of the posterior calcaneal tuberosity.
structures.function: Transmits calf force to the heel and stores elastic energy in running and jumping.
structures.baseball: Tendinopathy and rupture occur with explosive push-off and sprinting; load it progressively after time off.

structures.name: Plantar aponeurosis (plantar fascia)
structures.attachments: Medial calcaneal tuberosity to the plantar plates and flexor sheaths of the toes.
structures.function: Supports the longitudinal arch; tightens when the toes extend (windlass mechanism) to stiffen the foot for push-off.
structures.baseball: Plantar heel pain is common with high running volume and hard surfaces.

structures.name: Long plantar ligament
structures.attachments: Plantar calcaneus to the cuboid ridge and bases of the 2nd–5th metatarsals.
structures.function: Supports the lateral longitudinal arch and covers the fibularis longus tendon groove.

structures.name: Plantar plates (MTP joints)
structures.attachments: Thick fibrocartilage on the plantar side of each MTP joint, from the metatarsal neck to the base of the proximal phalanx.
structures.function: Limits toe hyperextension and supports the metatarsal heads.
structures.baseball: "Turf toe": a hyperextension sprain of the big-toe plantar plate, from push-off on firm turf or a forced toe-up position.
structures.note: All five plantar plates are selected together.

structures.name: Soleus
structures.origin: Back of the fibular head and upper fibula, soleal line and medial border of the tibia.
structures.insertion: Calcaneal tuberosity via the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon.
structures.action: Ankle plantarflexion at any knee angle; steadies the leg over the foot in stance.
structures.baseball: The main plantarflexor for running and drive-leg push; train it with bent-knee calf raises as well as straight-knee work.

structures.name: Plantaris
structures.origin: Lateral supracondylar line of the femur, above the lateral gastrocnemius head.
structures.insertion: Calcaneus, beside or with the calcaneal tendon.
structures.action: Weak plantarflexion and knee flexion.
structures.note: Absent in a minority of people.

structures.name: Tibialis anterior
structures.origin: Lateral condyle and upper lateral tibia, interosseous membrane.
structures.insertion: Medial cuneiform and base of the first metatarsal.
structures.action: Dorsiflexion and inversion; lowers the forefoot under control after heel contact.
structures.baseball: Pulls the toes up as the lead leg swings toward foot strike.

structures.name: Tibialis posterior
structures.origin: Posterior tibia, interosseous membrane and posterior fibula.
structures.insertion: Navicular tuberosity, cuneiforms, cuboid and bases of the 2nd–4th metatarsals.
structures.action: Inversion and plantarflexion; the main dynamic support of the medial arch.
structures.baseball: Controls lead-foot pronation as the foot takes load after foot strike.

structures.name: Fibularis (peroneus) longus
structures.origin: Fibular head and upper lateral fibula.
structures.insertion: Medial cuneiform and base of the first metatarsal, after crossing the sole.
structures.action: Eversion and plantarflexion; presses the first ray down and supports the transverse arch.
structures.baseball: Its quick reaction resists the roll-in of an inversion sprain.

structures.name: Fibularis (peroneus) brevis
structures.origin: Lower lateral fibula.
structures.insertion: Tuberosity at the base of the fifth metatarsal.
structures.action: Eversion and plantarflexion.
structures.baseball: An inversion sprain can pull its attachment off the fifth metatarsal base (avulsion fracture).

structures.name: Fibularis (peroneus) tertius
structures.origin: Lower anterior fibula.
structures.insertion: Dorsal base of the fifth metatarsal.
structures.action: Dorsiflexion and eversion.
structures.note: Absent in some people.

structures.name: Extensor digitorum longus
structures.origin: Lateral tibial condyle, upper anterior fibula and interosseous membrane.
structures.insertion: Middle and distal phalanges of toes 2–5 via the extensor expansions.
structures.action: Extends toes 2–5; dorsiflexion and eversion.

structures.name: Extensor hallucis longus
structures.origin: Middle anterior fibula and interosseous membrane.
structures.insertion: Base of the distal phalanx of the big toe.
structures.action: Extends the big toe; dorsiflexion.

structures.name: Flexor digitorum longus
structures.origin: Posterior tibia below the soleal line.
structures.insertion: Bases of the distal phalanges of toes 2–5.
structures.action: Flexes toes 2–5; plantarflexion and inversion; supports the arch.

structures.name: Flexor hallucis longus
structures.origin: Lower posterior fibula and interosseous membrane.
structures.insertion: Base of the distal phalanx of the big toe.
structures.action: Flexes the big toe; plantarflexion; supports the medial arch.
structures.baseball: Drives the big toe into the ground at the end of push-off and sprint stance.

structures.name: Abductor hallucis
structures.origin: Medial process of the calcaneal tuberosity, flexor retinaculum and plantar aponeurosis.
structures.insertion: Medial base of the proximal phalanx of the big toe.
structures.action: Abducts and flexes the big toe; supports the medial arch.
structures.baseball: Part of the foot "core" that holds the arch while the drive foot pushes.

structures.name: Flexor digitorum brevis
structures.origin: Medial process of the calcaneal tuberosity and plantar aponeurosis.
structures.insertion: Middle phalanges of toes 2–5.
structures.action: Flexes toes 2–5; supports the arch.

regions.name: Shoulder
regions.subtitle: Glenohumeral joint: cuff, prime movers, labrum and capsular ligaments
regions.prompt: Hide the deltoid, then trace each cuff tendon to its tubercle. Switch to Ligaments and find the inferior glenohumeral ligament: which band tightens in the late-cocking position?

regions.name: Scapula & clavicle
regions.subtitle: Scapulothoracic control, AC and SC joints
regions.prompt: Find the three muscles of the upward-rotation force couple. Which one pulls the inferior angle forward around the rib cage?

regions.name: Elbow & forearm
regions.subtitle: UCL, collateral ligaments and the flexor–pronator mass
regions.prompt: Select the UCL, then show the muscles. Which two muscles sit directly over its anterior bundle?

regions.name: Trunk & core
regions.subtitle: Rotation, anti-extension and the lumbopelvic link
regions.prompt: Follow the external oblique fibers down and forward. Which side’s internal oblique works with it to turn the trunk?

regions.name: Hip & pelvis
regions.subtitle: Hip capsule ligaments, glutes, deep rotators and adductors
regions.prompt: Lead-hip internal rotation: which capsular ligament tightens, and which muscles must lengthen to allow it?

regions.name: Thigh & knee
regions.subtitle: Hamstrings, quadriceps, cruciates, collaterals and menisci
regions.prompt: Compare the two biceps femoris heads: only one crosses the hip. Then find the ACL and say which tibial motion it limits.

regions.name: Ankle & foot
regions.subtitle: Lateral and medial ankle ligaments, the syndesmosis, calf and foot muscles
regions.prompt: Select the ATFL, CFL and PTFL in turn. Which one is tight when the foot is pointed down and turned in, the classic sprain position?
